reviewText: I will never buy again from this seller - Micca Distributor. They do not operate their business with integrity and they have no concern for their customers. reviewText: Purchased as a spare part, failed after first use. Works briefly if you tap on it... makes sparks. This is one of those projects that takes an hour the first time, but is a snap from then on. I have done it about 5 times and have it down to about 10 minutes. You may have to cut off an existing plastic connector and use the included high-temperature wire nuts. Our oven sees daily use and we have to replace this part every 12-18 months. I keep a spare on hand because it is, by far, the weak link in the design. If anything goes wrong with the oven, failure to light, smelling gas at startup, I change out this part first. Note, just because it is glowing does not mean it is working. The gas valve will only open if the element draws a very specific amount of electrical current, and the element can be slightly high or low and the valve will not open, even though it seems to be glowing properly.

reviewText: This is an update to a review I posted. My most recent purchase of the PLA PRO was not as successful, perhaps it's just a marginal batch? On my direct drive Makergear M2 I have been experiencing repeated jams. This is a machine that has been super reliable up until now. I cleaned the path, adjusted the gripper, replaced the nozzle -- in short everything one does with a clogged path. Then on the next run it would jam again 1/2 way through the job. I went back to Hatchbox and the same job has already run perfectly (as always). I wonder if the quality control at eSun isn't what it ought to be. Here's my original review: I've been shopping the various $20 (give or take) PLA products, been mostly using Hatchbox. Until now. This latest release from eSun is the most consistently good PLA I've seen, comparing favorably with some $40/kg PLA that my school uses. I also particularly like the fact that the finished parts have more of a satin finish rather than that excessively glossy finish I get with all of the other brands I've used. When I say consistent, I mean that when I print a part there's almost no uneven streaking on the sides of the part. At this point the output is getting very close to injection molded. My congrats to eSun, they have a long-term customer assuming they don't mess up. Highly recommend.

reviewText: iOS version review. 3 stars for now 12/19 I received the iOS version today, and used it with an iPhone 5 on the latest iOS version. pros: - size. it's tiny - seems very solid. But there's one moving part inside, the shutter for the lens to do the calibration. So a solid external case doesn't mean this should be dropped on the ground. - relatively high resolution (really high for the price) - price (from manufacturer). - value for this price. - no need for a battery. This uses the phone's battery. It's both a plus and a minus, but as long as your phone is charged, you can use the device without first charging an extra battery... - nice packaging, great carrying case included. cons: - noise level is quite high. (i.e. somewhat low quality images) - no spec about the sensitivity. i.e. does it detect a difference of 0.20 degrees C? 0.15? 0.10? better? Flir and other give that data, not Seek Thermal. IF the sensitivity is pretty bad, that can also explain the noise level. - big gradient on the screen. say point it at the floor. On my device (same on so many others), the bottom left corner will be about 6-7F warmer than the top right corner. Point at the floor and move around so now what was top is bottom, but you point at the same area on the floor. Same difference between lower left of the screen and top right of the screen. (you can turn any direction, the same difference will exist). So far, some tech guys on a forum seem to have found that to be an issue with the shutter (the clicking noise every second) that might not close fully/perfectly on top of the sensor. so each time the shutter closes to calibrate the sensor, the sensor would calibrate on something that is a gradient of temperature, therefore applying it to the image that is later on measured. IF that gradient is mostly identical between devices, the opposite gradient could be applied by software, at least for the photos. For videos, that might take too much time/calculations. Either way, this is a major issue with what is otherwise a great product. If Seeks Thermal fixes it, more stars will be added. Else, the reviews will be bad and the device eventually sell poorly . I would have expected the factory calibration procedures to take care of that. Hopefully every device was calibrated and the numbers are stored in each device already to enable a good software fix. If not, let's hope the SDK comes out quickly (and not just for Android but for iOS). - the software is below alpha quality for now on iOS. (and Android reports are not much better). For instance: there is no way to set the emissivity of materials. This is basic stuff for IR cameras and knowing what it uses would at least be the minimum. Changing it would come next. The Android version seems to have the feature but some folks claim changing the settings does nothing. It's not clear how much the users understand that concept and the limitations / physics of IR cameras... Taking photos doesn't seem to work, there is no feedback most of the time, but in fact the photos are taken "most of the time". They just do not reflect in the gallery miniature. Videos recording: one out of 4 or 5 times, I will get a message that the video failed to be saved. I've over 5GB of free space... So not being able to save a video mean some wasted time. (solution: save often by stop recording, then start again so not as much time is wasted to redo the measurements). Measure of the temperature where the user touches on the screen would be great. We have touch screens for a reason :-). Center temperature is ok, but if you attache the phone on a tripod, being able to check the temperature of something by just touching the screen would be great instead of moving the camera. Then you need a different account to post a question to their faq/support site. Then on the device you find out that you need to create some new credentials. At the very least I found that some special characters will result in the username/password to not be accepted. So you need something "quite simple". It's mostly showing the same images one has on the web site. - support forums: what support forums? There are very few FAQ, and that's about it. Any question has to be approved, and so far they do not seem to approve new stuff. I'm hoping for an open forum (with moderators, but not censors) soon. The is such a joke that on their support page they have 0 feature requests, and 0 questions. Really? The reality is that they have not approved anything to be posted. So start at 5 stars, remove 1.5 for the sensor gradient problem. Then 1 more star for the software not progressing fast enough (Android SW was out for a while. I know Apple take a long time to approve apps, but GooglePlay is fast), as well as the absence of good forums. I rounded it up to 3 stars :-) This is a new product, from what seems to be a new company, so I expect some pain/growing pains, and I'm looking forward to increase the rating here as they fix the problems. reviewText: This review is for the 32 ounce size, which is priced at about $17 as I write this review. Chlorine dioxide is a very effective virucide, fungicide, deodorizer, sanitizer, etc. I have been using chlorine dioxide sprays for years and much prefer them to bleach solutions, and other broad spectrum antimicrobials. But I have a couple of concerns about Performacide. My first problem is that a quart just doesnt fit into my use patterns and the way this Performacide is mixed doesnt allow for any flexibility. The instructions tell you not to open the pre-measured pouch. You just place the long, slim, sealed paper container into the spray bottle along with 32 ounces of water. Over the next hour, the sodium chlorite and other ingredients react to become chlorine dioxide. Once the chlorine dioxide is activated, the Performacide has to be used within 15 days. So, in planning your use of this product, you have to remember to allow an hour for the solution to activate and you have to remember to use it up within about two weeks. My need for a solution like this is either for a large amount (several gallons in the chicken coop) or for a very small amount (an ounce or so in the house cleaning up after the dog and cats). So the lack of flexibility in amount prepared and requirement to use it up within a couple of weeks don't work for me. My second concern is about price, which I ordinarily would not mention. You can do price comparisons as well as I can and prices on Amazon change regularly anyway. But it was not easy for me to find a chlorine dioxide spray that could be activated in varying quantities and is reasonably priced, so I want to bring your attention to Oxine AH (available on Amazon, etc.). Just like Performacide, Oxine begins as sodium chlorite and gets activated into chlorine dioxide and diluted as your needs dictate. But Oxine is available in a gallon container that can be activated and diluted to produce the equivalent of 780 quarts of Performacide. All for the price of about two quarts of Performacide. If you have a big project, or smaller projects that must be done periodically, the Oxine creates quite a savings. I like both products, although I prefer a multi-gallon sprayer with an easily activated wand rather than a hand-tiring trigger sprayer like Performacide provides. And both products require a great deal of caution in their use. Note that Performacide warns on the side of the bottle, among other things, that This product is not to be used in households or anywhere young children may be present. Finally, its essential to familiarize yourself with the OSHA and NIOSH standards for using the products.

reviewText: The fist thing I printed with this was a spool holder to mount this spool on my Afinia printer. These spools are cardboard with an odd center, it has a ridge in the middle of the spool so you need a notch in your spool holder. I posted the holder I designed on Thingiverse (add /thing:99383 after the URL, I can't post a link here), feel free to use or modify as you need. Anyway, the sides of the spool are right at the level of the filament so as someone else mentioned, it tends to fall off the spool (as seen in the product photo). I left it alone for an hour last night and it tied itself around the spool holder and jammed up. I had to toss a couple of hours of printing but luckily the nozzle is ok. The filament seems to print ok, maybe not quite as nice as the other brands of filament I've used. I'm using the low temperature setting on the Afina (I have this on the printer  Extruder Nozzle Temperature Switch for Afinia and UP! 3D Printers ). [update] After printing about half the spool worth, I'd say this filament is inferior to some premium filament I have, but there's a chance that it needs a different temperature than normal ABS. In any case, other brands are about the same price and work better for me so I will switch to them.

reviewText: As microscope slides and coverslips go, they do what they should. I use them for hobby microscopy. The edges and corners are not finished very well, but they are not sharp either (no cuts yet). Don't expect them to be squeaky clean at this price - they have a little paper lint, and something a bit tacky, on the surfaces - a good rub with a little alcohol on a Kimwipe or microfiber is needed before using. The little plastic container that holds the coverslips isn't quite deep enough, so watch out when you first open it, or the top 10 or so will fall right on the floor. It's kinda hard to get apart, so be careful. Will likely order same brand again when needed.

reviewText: I own a 12" Brown & Sharpe caliper in thousandths of an inch, which looks and feels like the sort of instrument a company like Apple or Mercedes would produce. A great deal of thought went into its design, and you can see it in the details. This caliper by Oshlun is not of that caliber, but it is extremely good and works without flaw. Its accuracy is absolute. More than one reviewer commented that the feel was not right. One said it was gravely, and another said there was a "hump" in the action. I experience neither. The action is silky smooth without any rough spots over its entire range. The needle always goes back to zero. (the dial is adjustable if for some reason it needs it) In fact, the instrument seems to be an exact copy of one by Fowler (in .02 mm markings), but this one is in fractions of an inch. It copies the better instrument very closely, with only a few differences, but those differences are enough to feel that it's not in the same class as those more expensive instruments. It's about half the price, too. So, what we have is an instrument that looks and almost feels like those costing twice as much to 5 times as much, and is really just as accurate as those. It has sharper corners, more likely to snag something, and maybe ever so slightly less "tight" in its action, but it is still very smooth, very well-machined, and does not disappoint. If I did not have the more expensive instruments with which to compare it, I would never know that it was possible to make one better. What I'm saying is that this is a fine measuring tool that will never wear out, always will measure accurately, and will not disappoint. It is impressive to see, to hold, and to use. There is no reason to avoid it; it's a fine tool for a good price. It requires no batteries, and its dial is always easy to read. It also has tenths of an inch on its scale, so it's a dual-scale device. It also has millimeters on the shaft, but not on the dial. I use this a lot, in spite of the finer calipers I own. I'm not afraid to drop it or use it where it could get dirty, because it's NOT the more expensive one. And... the results are exactly the same as if I were using the Brown & Sharpe. I guess the Brown & Sharpe reads more accurately, since its scale is 10 times the sensitivity of this one, but this is still a great instrument.

reviewText: The first thing I noticed when I open the box is that this machine was made with good quality materials and it is sturdy enough to last for years, while doing harsh cleaning jobs. Its a perfect timing for us because were remodeling our home and there is dust everywhere. But I will be using it all around the year to pick the sand that is all over our place, because we live half a block from the beach. Since this machine functions as a vacuum and as a blower, this year cleaning the front and back porch should be easier. I cant wait to blow away all those leaves instead of sweeping them with a broom. The design in this vacuum is similar to other dry/wet vacuums Id used in the past, in this particular model I like the size of it, the easy way to operate it, and the wheels. Our previous unit didn't have wheels, which was uncomfortable. This Porter-Cable wet dry vacuum comes with useful accessories like wide extension wands, a disposable dust bag, floor nozzle, and utility nozzle. Of these attachments, my favorite is the floor nozzle, which has two removable bottom blades. One is a rubber squeegee, I guess for wet floors cleaning. And the other is like a thin blade with a series of small brushes in it. For dry floor cleaning, I learned that removing the squeegee allows a smoother cleaning. A flexible hose, and cartridge filter are also included, but this is common with most dry/wet vac machines. I would have liked to try the wet vacuum features of this Porter-Cable wet dry vacuum, but the foam filter was not included in the unit I received. Yes, is printed in the box and in the manual that it was included, but regardless of that, it was not. And in the manual is stated that this machine needs the previously mentioned foam filter for vacuuming liquid. So, I will have to order a foam filter the next time I place an order, because its a good thing to have it in the event of a mild flood, which we often get at the shore during storms. Summing up, this is a good machine for tough cleaning jobs.

reviewText: This digital caliper is very nice considering the price. Don't waste your money on the cheap Harbor Freight ones, buy this instead...it's a much higher quality unit. It's moisture resistant and comes with an extra battery. This caliper could definitely be used for reference inspection of production parts. The "Pro Quality" description is not an exaggeration. The only thing I wish it had was a backlight that would come on for say 10 seconds and then turn off. I know you should always use this in a well lit area but sometimes I just want to do a quick measurement and there are moments where the ambient lighting is not ideal so a backlight would be nice to have.

reviewText: I've had this printer for about three months now, and while it hasn't been used much recently, I've been happy with it. I ran it almost every day the first month I had it, and it sat in my basement unused until early last week. It still ran fine despite literally being dusty from sitting there. I want to share a few experiences from this printer. First, I haven't had to contact Flashforge for assistance, but I did send an email requesting some general tips for printing. I got a very quick response from Tang. Second, I read some now-outdated information that gave tips on "touching off" the printer's nozzle and leveling the build plate. On this unit, there is no need to touch off as long as you home the machine (which it'll do if you switch filaments or level the plate), and leveling the plate is easy; Tighten three screws under the plate, the probe next to the nozzle flicks down and measures the distance, and the printer will either tell you to tighten or loosen the corresponding screw, or it'll say it's fine and move to the next location. I think this is great for new users, particularly those who are unfamiliar with automated manufacturing technology. Finally, the part that I struggled with: Loading the filament. Once the nozzle heats up, you're prompted to press a spring loaded lever on the head to allow the filament to be loaded into the nozzle. I pressed down on that lever firmly, which caused the filament to bind and not load into the nozzle. After experimenting, I learned that you shouldn't be forceful with that lever as I was. When prompted, slowly press the lever down while trying to GENTLY push the filament into the loading tube. As soon as the filament slides down the tube, STOP pressing that spring loaded lever down, and hold it at the position it's at. Once the nozzle starts drawing the filament in without you pressing it in, and/or you see melted filament coming out of the nozzle, you're all set and free to release the spring loaded lever. I know that at this time there's cheaper 3D printers on the market, but this is the one I'd recommend. Again, I think it's so user friendly that even those who unfamiliar with operating automated equipment will pick this up well. And while I haven't used this machine non-stop for months or owned it for years, I feel pretty good about the quality of it as a entry level machine.

reviewText: I have had so much fun with these 11 different tapes and while I have not emptied the kit's contents, yet, I find them especially useful. 1. Safety Walk Tape: This tape was the first installed and it is a lifesaver or at least it is an accident preventer for the two old foggies here. Our indoor garage stoop has two steps that are consistently attempting to trip our entry and exit; however, with these our incidence of trips are and will be eliminated or at least reduced significantly. 2. Masking Corner Tape: With all the wet weather we have been having, I have yet to use these; however, based on the design and means of application, I can tell they should do the job as intended. Should that not be the case, I will amend this as soon as spring begins. 3. Foam Removable Tape: These did not last too long. The plastic coupled with the tape made a perfect presentation aid for mounting borderless pictures among other display items that do not require extreme holding properties. With a modicum of pre-planning, each strip can be cut to a more satisfactory length depending on the item. 4. Quick Grab Tape: I used several of these for those light objects that I wanted to hold items in place and they work well. 5. (Blue) and 6. (Red): Vinyl Duct Tape: Granny used to say 'A home is not no home with no Duct tape' but she did not mention that this Duct Tape is a top quality Duct Tape. Back then, the issue of quality was almost non-existent. You either had duct tape that was gray or silver colored and that's it. But I do not know, since I did not own duct tape until the id 60's. This tape, unlike some of the others, offers solid sticking power and since it is two colors it makes for quick item identification. 7. Reflective Tape: I am saving this until spring except just to be sure its reflective quality met minimum standards, I used a piece on the mailbox for test purposes and it works quite well. 8. Wire Management Tape: These tapes are just the product for those of us who have more exposed wires running behind and under all sorts of furniture and stuff. It is almost a nightmare if you think about 'now where does that wire go...?' or the likes. These 2 different colored tapes can help with managing those issues with ease. 9. Dual Lock Reclosable Fastener: Take lightweight items and mount them in a locally suitable position and add organization to an otherwise unorganized spot or several. I have a spot for the house keys and vehicle remotes as well as other little helpers and love them. 10. Hook and Loop Pieces: I only used a couple of these so far and that was to adhere each piece to a curtain that covers the infrared camera positioned to keep track of wildlife and civilized visitors. If I need to make any curtain adjustment, all I have to do is remove the tape and refit or change the SD card for the camera. 11. Command Strips: These hooks are absolutely fantastic and work well. I bought my first set of two several years ago and they are still working just as well as they did in the beginning. That is after may a hanging of my heavy outdoors coats. These are no different and will get even more use in the garage. I already claimed my spot for the next mounting and cannot wait until the weather warms some. First, it is 3M and that makes a positive difference to me. They work as intended and work well. The pieces together form a 5 star rating; however, I chose a 4 star for a couple of minor reasons. Most of the comments are objective and some are, frankly, subjective. I saw the kit as an introduction of many around the home tapes and potential uses without a large supply of any particular tape. If a particular piece runs out and it will, it is readily reorderable from the handy enclosed tape description sheet. Their Guide Map shows where each tape should be located in the box (a handy kit and container while being somewhat larger). The one addition I would make as soon as possible is an identifier on each roll or piece of tape. The existing rolls and items do not have any code or written information on the inside of the roll. I am delighted with the 3M Kit and will soon be seeking a replacement for many of the contents and highly recommend the products of 3M.

reviewText: I wanted the Glow in the Dark filament to make toys for my young nephew. I had not used Hatchbox filament before but it was a competitive price and available from Fire Sale Merchants with my Amazon Prime. It arrived promptly and I loaded it in my printrbot Simple Metal to try it. It comes loaded on a plastic reel with with a 1 1/4in/32.2mm hole in the hub. The reel has the usual inspection hole in the side so you can see when you are almost out. It is labeled as 1.75mm plus or minus .05mm but I measured it in 5 places and it was spot on at 1.75mm at each place. The filament ran cleanly through the extruder and extruded smoothly. I used a 200C heat setting and was very satisfied. I had no problems getting to adhere to the print bed. It truely glows in the dark. I printed a Star Wars bust for my nephew and he uses it as a night light. I am very happy with the product and intend to buy more Hatchbox filament. I was also very happy with Fire Sale Merchant as a vendor. They even contacted me to make sure I got what I wanted. Bruce Buchner

I find that it's not always the best product for breaking heavy rust and corrosion or preserving metal outdoors for extended periods, but it is still a very good all around general purpose spray lubricant for many tasks and I always have several cans of it on hand at any given time.

I use the 2" brads to hold together small butt-jointed paint grade boxes. I could probably go shorter, say 1 5/8" or even 1 3/4"; but to be honest the 2" brads were the cheapest and work perfectly fine for my use with no blowouts, misfires or jams, which can occur with nails of lesser quality. reviewText: This shop vacuum deserves a five star rating based on performance, but the company has managed to save money by having no quality control system. Mine arrived with two incorrect parts and had I noticed the problem at the early stages, I would have packed it up and returned it. But I was well into assembly by the time I recognized the problems. The most serious problem involved the factory installation of two left wheel locks in stead of one left and one right wheel lock. As one can see in the pictures below, both wheel locks have the step plate going in the same direction. I did not notice this problem until I completed installation of the left wheel and upon adding the right wheel noticed it would not go all the way in because the wheel lock had the step going towards instead of away from the wheel (see the second picture below). I solved the problem by cutting off the section that extends towards the wheel and it still works just fine. But the consumer should not be required to do remanufacturing to get things to work. The second problem was that only one of the wheel nuts that was included was a lock nut. The others were all regular nuts and a lock nut is required to hold the wheel on as a regular nut, if tightened down, would prevent the wheel from turning. A lock nut can be tightened just enough to keep the wheel on while allowing for free rotation. I solved the problem by using a thread sealer that served to hold the nut in place. After suffering through assembly, I then used the Shop Vac to clean the basement floor and the work room. It worked beautifully, and was very impressive in terms of suction and the extensions and attachments were of high quality. Indeed, the 8 foot hose is the best vacuum hose I have every seen. Thus, I gave the unit 5 stars for performance and 3 stars for pain and suffering during assembly. My strong recommendation is that you carefully check all the parts including the installed parts and if anything is missing, return it to Amazon for replacement. It is very hard to tell through the plastic whether you have a lock nut or a regular nut, however. But the lock nuts are a lot thicker and have small round marks on two faces which are indentations to make the nut hard to turn on the screw. The company should be dinged for using such a cheap lock nut, and dinged even more for not including the right number. Fortunately, if you or going to buy a shop vac from a company with no quality control, Amazon is a great place to buy such a thing because replacement is so easy. It is unfortunate that something that works so well once assembled is shipped without paying attention to the details, but I still recommend this item because it works so well. It is very solidly built, and moving it up and down the stairs is quite easy because of the design, excellent handle and large rear wheels. Storing all the attachments inside is also very convenient. In summary, just make sure you have all the parts before starting to assemble. And for the cretin who will invariably add a comment that I am the fool for not checking the parts before assembling, I was indeed partially to blame. Let this review prepare you for the fact that this company seems to lack quality control during assembly and parts preparation. But once you get the thing put together, this is indeed a 5 star shop vac.

reviewText: This was easy to put together, and it was easy to fill with hot water and the enclosed cleaning solution. It sucks up the water thoroughly (not leaving it soggy wet) and it cleaned the carpets really well. It only has the one tank where you mix the hot water and the cleaning solution together, but the tank is large enough to finish an entire room (where we previously have had to refill once or twice to finish our living room). The brushes seem to work really well and you could see where you had run the machine over the carpet, and where you had not. This helped make the carpet feel softer after the entire process was done. We vacuum the carpet, run the shampoo over the carpet with the cleaning solution, and then using a tank of just hot water, run the machine one more time, let the carpet dry and then vacuum. It looks great when it's done, and since it sucks up the water really well it dries quicker than other machines we have used. The cord did not get hot during use. It is a simple, sturdy carpet cleaner with no bells or whistles, but does exactly as advertised.

reviewText: I love the design on this shop vacuum. The wall mount is a great feature, especially in the garage when coupled with the 21' hose length. A thick plastic mounting plate is easy to attach to the wall and from there, it's simple to hang the vacuum. There are two hoses than combine to get the 21' length. You can reach a good distance with the 20' cord length as well, so between the length of the hose and the power cord, you can cover a lot of area. The hose is 2" in diameter and can suck up good size debris. RIGID makes a few different filter types for different uses. Mine is just for standard vacuuming, so I don't have need for the fine particle filters, etc. Still, it's nice to have that option. It comes with the Utility Nozzle, Dusting Brush, 2 Extension Wands, Car Nozzle (with LED light), Crevice Tool, Diffuser, One Qwik Lock Filter, a 14 Foot Hose and a 7 Foot Hose - and again - both hoses can be hooked together. One hose is a 14' Tug-a-Long and the other is a 7' expanding hose. It's not too loud, it sounds as loud as our air conditioning unit, so not quiet, but not too bad. The suction power is very strong, even with both hoses in use. It's a reasonably priced shop vacuum that has a lot of great features, plus is has a lifetime warranty against material defects and workmanship.

reviewText: After doing as much research as I could, I settled on this unit and pulled the trigger on Wednesday - two days before Christmas. I paid the extra for two day shipping knowing the holidays would probably screw things up, but lo and behold, the printer showed up THE VERY NEXT DAY to my door. I was stoked! Go Amazon PRIME! Having read all the reviews with bitches, gripes, and complaints I dove into the box of parts on Thursday evening. I went through the inventory checklist and made sure the big items were there, some I couldn't identify because I didn't know what I was looking at, some there were too many (like screws) and I just said "Screw it! There's enough screws". I was a little disturbed that I did NOT receive the CD with Cura or the other stuff, but hey.... I'm a progenitor of the Interweb and EVERYTHING is out there to be found, right? With a little searching I found the complete set of manuals, assembly instructions, FAQ, etc. and had them downloaded in nothing at the speed of megabit. There were several times that I would look and look for something and go "AHA! They screwed me out that piece!" only to find out I was wrong and it was in another little baggy somewhere. The parts are grouped logically by assembly section and many times there were extras too. Plenty of extra screws and nuts of all the sizes so when one would fly off the table into the black hole that eats small parts, all was not lost. I'm sure my vacuum cleaner will announce their presence very soon. I will have to admit that I'm mystified at what some people call "misleading" or "inaccurate" instructions. It's a bunch of pictures with a little text to point you in the right direction. How hard can that be? Of course, I know grown men today who are tentative at even changing a flat tire on a car - another thing that has mystified me as much as we are a "driven" culture. So with the assembly diagrams in front of me, I pulled out one part at a time and starting putting it together at a leisurely pace. I also wrapped presents, took phone calls, coordinated dinner at the same time so it's not like there weren't distractions. I think total time for assembly with all this going on took maybe 12 hours and it was fun and easy, easy, easy. I had to look at some of the diagrams a few times because I had never built anything like this before and I had to understand what that piece does. Could the instructions be better? Sure, if you wanted to have a document that looked like a War & Peace novel, and even that would probably be so verbose with Chingrish you would end up more confused than ever! I've written a manual or two in my day and there is ALWAYS something that get's lost in the translation, so just take your time and study the drawings and it'll come to you. If you need to take a break from it, go to the InnerTube and watch a video of it in operation, you'll see how it all works. With all that said, did it go together perfect? Nope. There were plenty of times that ignored the few words on the diagrams and grabbed the wrong part - like using the 295mm aluminum pieces when I should have used the 308mm pieces and then the hotbed plate wouldn't fit on the slides. DOH! I had to take it all apart and use the right pieces and it fit perfectly. With everything that was going on, I still managed to do rough calibration and setup and printed my first Ultimaker Robot on the 26th at around noon. Not bad for an old fart! The only real beef I had with the kit is the Y axis idler pulley is actually just a 608 bearing. The belt doesn't center itself well on this flat pulley and will start binding on the bearing bracket/post. This will translate to difficult movement of the "Y" axis as the belt tracks from one side to the other and it "drifts back and forth in full transit. A proper, toothed, timing pulley with a bearing would solve this problem for good and even allow for a little offset if you didn't get it centered exactly. Suggestions - To tbe buyer and the manufacturer Buyer - Invest in a nice set of ball end allen wrenches that are longer than the ones that come with the kit. There are some positions that require a slight angle access after assembly that will make good use of them. Unless you buy a cheap crappy set, they will be much more durable than the ones that come with the kit. Buyer - Everyone seems to have a problem getting the toothed belt locked into the carrier. Use a pair of needle nose pliers to hold one side while starting the short side in the carrier. If you stretch it a bit with the pliers and push in, it will start better. Use the small flat screw driver to push it in the rest of the way. Manufacturer - As above, the allen wrenches are adequate for assembly, but do start rounding off with just one or two slips. A little better set of these would go a long way. You could even lose the little side cutter pliers to offset since you only use those for one step - stripping wire ends. Manufacturer - use a proper toothed pulley on the "Y" axis idler. The "X" axis idler bearing has a narrow guideway that keeps it centered and it doesn't have the "drift" problems that the "Y" axis does. Buyer - get a nice small 300mm ruler or scale - comes in handy. Conclusion : If the CD had been in the box, chances are I would have given it a 5 across the board. This unit has the largest print volume available on a kit and the aluminum frame is the way to go vs. acrylic or wood. Once you get the unit trimmed up and calibrated, you can print replacement parts and smooth things up if you so desire. The water jet cut parts are perfect and fit very nicely, and when the protective paper is removed add to the finish of the printer. I have had a ton of the 80/20 aluminum extrusions, linear slides, and some bigger stepper motors kicking around in my shop for years. I'm thinking I could duplicate this unit easily on a much bigger scale and maybe go to an 18" or even 24" hot bed with dual extruders. That would be SAWEET!

reviewText: This is a fairly good product I've used it for a multitude of repairs. It's great for repairing toys especially. I've glued my daughters 3" "Kristof" figure who's head broke off. I've repairs a 3" "Flynn Rider" who had a leg/hip replacement which required a small steel pin and a touch of gorilla glue. I've also used it on a 3" "Dragons" "Heather" figure who's body broke in two, she too required a steel pin and a drop or two of Gorilla Glue. This glue doesnt work particularly well in areas which are continually subjected to moisture however I have successfully repaired my daughters watering can as well... Ill post additional photos as Im able to in updates. TIP: when repairing small figures you will need a heavy/large paper clip, pair of "dyke" pliers which also have a wire cutting edge, a drill with a small drill bit almost the same size of the paper clip in circumference. From there you will need to drill each direction creating a cavity in the area which you are repairing to allow the pre-measured/cut paper clip piece you've prepared for the "steel pin" used to give extra strength to the figure in the repaired area. Insert a small drop in each piece of the toy to be rejoined and then run the part under water allowing the water to hit the drop of gorilla glue (water activates the glue), insert the piece of paper clip which you've pre-cut/pre-measured into the cavity which you've placed the drop of Gorilla Glue and connect both parts to be joined. You will need a small clamp or a piece of strong packing tape to hold the joined pieces together while drying as the glue does EXPAND. I like to take a wet paper towel after about 5-10 min and when I see the glue expanding outward pack it down with the wet paper towel crushing all the bubbles which start during the activation of the glue as it dries so ther is a smoother area after drying. I'll at times take a matching sharpie and after the glued area is dry, I will color the glued area with the sharpie to mask the area which was repaired. SEE MY PHOTOS OF A RECENT REPAIR DONE EARLIER TODAY. I've also used this glue on floor tiles in a commercial building as a quick repair alternative to adhesive/mortar or mastic etc. see photos, they aren't pretty until the glue is colored with a black/brown sharpie, then they look ok. The tile was shattered into many pieces and was loose until I cleaned the area, added some water for activation and then the glue, using a wet paper towel patting it down as it raised and dried. It was quick and able to be walked on in less than an hour. Threw a mat over it and It worked ok for a quick fix. This glue isn't perfect as it doesn't hold well for all repairs. However it's the best I've used and there are times which a stronger commercial adhesive is best for certain applications. Good luck with whatever your repairing, take your time these things take patients. reviewText: As many of you know, silver-based compounds are superior to silicone bases for CPU heat transfer. I can tell you that Arctic Silver 5 proves this to be the case. I read the customer reviews on Radio Shack's site and they all praised the RS silicone compound, but it does not work sufficiently for modern machines in my experience. I have an Intel I5 760 Quadcore processor with the stock intel heat sink. With the RS silicone base, I was getting CPU temps of 99C at 100% load! This is the core max temp and is obviously not good for the processor. I achieved this max temp within 30 seconds of running Prime95 torture test and within about 1 minute of running a heavy TIF file export out of Lightroom3. I needed a different solution. I tried dismounting the heatsink, reapplying the RS compound - same deal. (I applied properly with a thin layer, evenly spread). All to no avail. Ordered this Arctic Silver 5 stuff and immediately at application, the difference was obvious. It's extremely thick and spreads very evenly. I used a guitar pick and got it very thin and very even on the heat sink plate. I installed it and immediately ran the Prime95 torture test... Whereas I got to 99C in seconds before, I have been running the torture test now (it's still going as I write) for about 32 MINUTES and the core temps have not exceeded 85C! I will never use another thermal compound for my CPUs.

reviewText: I finally tracked down this package of three carpets and another smaller package after one and one-half days of looking, emailing, Amazon and UPS telling me my package had been delivered to my porch at 5:06 PM the day before etc., at a house number 586 while my house number is 566. One at my front entrance, one at the back french doors on the inside and one on the outside deck, where my husband stands to smoke. The inside one replaced a beautiful throw carpet which wrinkled when the door was opened and closed too often. I had previously order a smaller 2' x 3' carpet, the same as these, so that I already knew this was what I wanted. I placed the smaller carpet at the top of the deck stairs. I really like the "teeth" on the back that grab the carpet inside the house so that the 3' x 5' won't move. I particularly like the heavy rubber backing helping hold the carpets in place on the deck and the front porch entry. These are very substantial and look like they will last several years. The colors are as shown and I would describe the color as camel rather than medium brown.

reviewText: I know...they're squirt bottles. But hey, if you're here looking at them you were like me and probably needed some sprayers. In the past, I've used Rubbermaid, ZEP and a few other brands of sprayers. I won't say they were terrible, but I'm here purchasing more for one reason or another. First, these hold 32 ounces of fluid which may be more than you actually need or want. When fully, they are a little heavy. What I really like about them is they are clear, so I can see if whatever solution I have in them is, well, no longer in solution! A visual inspection is nice and it's easy to do with these unlike opaque or colored bottles. Second, the sprayer head itself has a very long trigger on it which makes it possible to wrap all your fingers on the trigger. This may not sound like much, but when you have a lot of spraying to do, it really lessens fatigue. Lastly, the pump is very stout and moves a high volume of fluid. The fine mist is saturating and the stream is more like a super soaker than a spray bottle! My two year old LOVES this setting. All in all, they are great to have on hand and they seem like they will last. I hope you found my review helpful and if so, please click the yes button below. Thanks!

reviewText: The HHIP 8401-0448 20" LED Waterproof Bolt on Work Light is an awesome work light. I'm wondering if some work needs to be done on the product name...HHIP 8401-0448. Hmm...sure the whole thing isn't bad "HHIP 8401-0448 20" LED Waterproof Bolt on Work Light". But anyway, on to the actual physical light. When I chose this to test, I thought it was just a regular clamp on style work light. Well when I got this I was impressed by the initial weight, which was quite hefty. Then I opened the box and was impressed by how industrial this work light appeared. The gooseneck is like a full finger width, which is quite substantial. The actual product gooseneck is more subtle than what you see in the product shots though but still a very robust gooseneck. Now because I love this work light, I'm not going to be dipping it in water to test the accuracy of the waterproof quality, I'll leave that up to happenstance. The lumens count at 330 is very adequate for what I am testing it with. It lights a room quite well with the ambient reflection but concentrates the beam nicely too. The on/off switch is located at the head or led array end.

reviewText: Works great. Being a novice to Arduino I had trouble modifying Marlin from watching YouTube videos and other commentary and reviews because of different versions of the library's and the Marlin program. I used Marlin-1.1.x and library item U8glib-1.19.1 on the Ramps 1.4 shield and Arduino MEGA 2560. When modifying Marlin in Arduino IDE, go to tab "Configuration.h", ignore line numbers and search (Ctrl+F) for "REPRAP_DISCOUNT_FULL_GRAPHIC_SMART_CONTROLLER", and remove the comment marks (//) in front of it. Also search for "REPRAP_DISCOUNT_SMART_CONTROLLER" and comment it out by adding "//" on the left side. Compile and load the code to your Arduino MEGA 2560 and Ramps 1.4. Power down and then power up again with the display attached, and be delighted with a functioning visual interface. Additionally, you have to enable SD Card support by searching for "SDSUPPORT" and removing the comment "//" on the left side. The SD Card now works great.

reviewText: The Pyrex brand made its name for heat-resistant, tough glassware based on borosilicate glass. They use a different, less-expensive formula now and breakage rates due to thermal stress fractures are up. I wanted 'something better/safer' and this is it. The crystal clear glass and easily read measurements are also a plus. The rolled rim is wide enough to serve as a hand grip for pouring. I use this for mixing liquids in the kitchen--eggs for omelets and batters. The high straight sides also work well with an immersion blender but the diameter is too small to use a standard egg beater for whipping heavy cream or egg whites. Don't use a heavy spoon with this--hitting the side of the beaker abruptly can cause breakage. Buy a laboratory stirrer instead or use plastic stirrers. I bought two of these and one is still going strong; my wife broke the other by vigorously whacking a spoon against the sides while making pancake batter. Outside dimensions are 5 1/4 inches tall and 4 inches across(including the nicely rolled rim.) The product is stable on a countertop. It is just the thing for mixing small batches of batter...and about as large a size as one would want for kitchen use.

reviewText: Anyone who has been around a lab or precision workshop is familiar with Kimwipes which are made from wood fiber and used to clean optics or precision mechanisms, whenever it's not acceptable to leave fibers behind as with ordinary paper towels. These Kimtex wipers are one step more high tech. These are not wood fiber or paper fiber but post-consumer polypropylene and work very well for cleaning up chemical spills, solvents, oils. Tough but soft and scratch free. If you don't know exactly the chemical makeup of your surface, or think it may be strongly acidic or basic, these are your best bet, very benign. I just used these with alcohol pads to clean up a 50 year old collector's camera. Did a nice job.

reviewText: I've tried just about every Velcro product on Amazon and most of them are ok to good but this particular Velcro is the BEST; the easiest to pick off the paper giving you a better grip. Talking about 'grip' this has it in spades. I don't know why but the black Velcro seems to be the toughest and much stronger than the white. I devised a turntable with sections for my many medications and each one is Velcroed so I can pop it off and then pop it on. Trying all of them the black is the easiest to 'hold' and all you have to do is 'push' the item in if it's something you use all the time; makes life easier and everything is right there. (First I glued little plastic bottles all around a larger plastic container and glued the whole thing on a turntable. Then Velcro the whole thing right to whatever space I had and then some!) I would also trust this Velcro for picture frames, remotes handy in the bedroom on side tables or dresser or on the TV itself; keeping pens available, notepads (light weight). It's one handy dandy product! There are l,0001 things you can do with Velcro and believe me I have the stuff in use all over the house-in the kitchen, in the bathroom, in the bedroom; just about everywhere. Think of things that you use everyday and wish you didn't have to search through drawers to find-Velcro them to a painted block of wood or whatever you choose and they are right there when you need them' push on-- push off! I also use Velcro on my desk-holds remotes, pens, most anything that you can think of (not to terribly heavy like a stapler or some such). One tip: Use the 'rough zipper' side on the wall or the product you're sticking something to and the soft side is the one you handle. The zipper side hurts; I found that out pretty quickly. Items stay on better and are easier to 'push in' when the zipper side is what the 'smooth' side is being pushed against...make sense? Well get your thinking cap on and I'm sure you'll think of a zillion ways this great product can help you. By the way; this same Velcro would be much more costly anywhere!! Update: I've just received two more boxes of Velcro. The price has gone up aprox. 3.00 ea. so I wasn't thrilled with that but I love and use Velcro all the time so I bought anyway. I have a few hats that are to big so I take either side of Velcro and press on the underside which helps keep the hat on, won't stay on... so it doesn't come off use a glue gun, that will make sure that stays on!

reviewText: Purchased in early April 2016 (almost two years ago), and put to use when received. Ive changed the Amazon Basics AA battery once, which I do with most of my battery-operated products every 6 or 12 months (especially with smoke detectors/alarms). I don't wait for batteries to die. I appreciate how quickly the readings are available. For instance, I can walk from one part of my first floor home to the other, and see the difference in temperature and humidity readings within seconds. The digital numbers are easy to read as long as I have on my glasses and Im not in the dark. Theres a tiny white button located on the back that les you choose Fahrenheit or Celsius. I would definitely buy this Acurite model again*. I paid $3 more in 2016. HOW ACCURATE ARE THE READINGS? I can tell if the readings are accurate by comparing different areas of my home where it is obvious (see messy images) that the humidity is really high. In Miami, FL, I doubt Ill ever witness a really low humidity reading room in my old home. I have a large window that needs to be replaced (the whole darn thing, glass and frame). It allows outside weather conditions (heat and more heat) to seep right into my home. Yep, already added that ugly and cheap plastic sheeting over the frame, but its not helping enough. WHY I BOUGHT THIS: I use this meter, mostly it seems, just to annoy myself. LOL! Im not using for growing indoor plants or any other casually scientific reason. I just like to know why I feel like crapnothing escapes the effects of dampness in the air, the dampness that can easily make me feel miserable, the dampness that requires me to cleanly wipe down even more crap. On a positive note, its easy to turn on the air conditioner (sometimes using the free air circulation) to help reduce these issues. Until I can find a person willing to empty bins of water for me every single day, I cant be bothered with dehumidifiers. Nobody in their right mind leaves stagnant water in Miami (mosquitos will find it). For those trying to learn the most basic humidity examples: Very low humidity can cause dry skin, nosebleeds, and who knows what else. Very high humidity can help improve plant growth, improve mold growth (you don't want that), but can also cause a person to feel uncomfortable and/or sweaty. (*) AcuRite 00613 Humidity Monitor with Indoor Thermometer, Digital Hygrometer and Humidity Gauge Indicator
